channel.title: Jumoo Releases
channel.description: Latest NuGet package releases from Jumoo

item.title: Publicis Connector 17.0.1
item.description:
### Changed
- The connector now logs why a Publicis job item isn't collected. An order with no items, or an item that isn't ready yet, is logged at Information with the order, item, language, job and status. An item that returns no file, or a translation that fails to load into the job, is logged as a Warning. Before this, those cases were skipped silently, so a job that never received its translation left nothing in the site's logs.
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Jumoo/TranslatePlus-Connector/compare/v17.0.0...v17.0.1

item.title: LanguageWire Connector 17.1.2

item.title: CrowdIn Connector 18.1.0
item.description:
### Added
- `IOptionsTranslationProvider.GetOptions(OptionsDetailLevel)` support — withholds the CrowdIn access token when only a partial view of the connector's options is needed (e.g. during job creation). - Repository standards: `LICENSE.txt`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `.editorconfig`, `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`, `GitVersion.yml`, `nuget.config`, dependabot, and issue and PR templates. - `nuget.config` pins the restore sources and adds package source mapping, so only `Jumoo.*` may come from the nightly feed and everything else comes from nuget.org. - CI workflows — PR build, package build, release, and CodeQL. The package build runs the client build before packing, so the produced package actually contains the backoffice assets. - Releases publish to NuGet from a `v{version}` tag pushed on a release branch, gated behind the `nuget` GitHub environment and authenticated with trusted publishing (OIDC) rather than a stored API key.
### Fixed
- `CrowdInComposer` now gates its registrations on the Umbraco backoffice being enabled, matching the check Translation Manager core applies in its own composers, so the connector no longer tries to register on a website-only boot.
### Changed
- Now requires Translation Manager 18.2.0 or later (`Jumoo.TranslationManager.Core` and `.Serializers`, previously 18.0.0).

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0-rc2
item.description:
### Added
- **Headless pipeline runs.** `IPipelineRunner` starts a pipeline in one call - created as a background request, options applied, posted to the processing queue - and returns once it is queued. Over the API: `POST StartPipeline` (`202` with the pipeline id and a status URL, `409` with the running pipeline's id when the concurrency key is held), `GET PipelineStatus/{id}` and `POST CancelPipeline/{id}`. Status reports `Queued`/`Running`/`Scheduled`/`Waiting`/`Completed`/ `Failed`/`Cancelled`; `complete` is only true once the run has finished (a `Waiting` run has not), and errors carry the message, action and step but no stack trace. - **Cancel.** A new `Cancelled` pipeline status (added at the end of `PipelineStatus`, so existing values don't move) and a `CancelRequested` flag on the pipeline state. Cancel is cooperative: it takes effect before the next step, and the strategy's clean runs. The `@jumoo/processing` client treats `Cancelled` like `Failed`. `PipelineCleanupJob` removes cancelled pipelines along with completed and failed ones, and never removes waiting ones. - **Concurrency keys.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetConcurrencyKey(strategy, options)` (default `null`). Every way of starting a pipeline gets the processor's key; while one pipeline holding a key is `Running`, `Background` or `Scheduled`, another with the same key is refused, and a `Waiting` one can't resume. Stored in a new indexed `ConcurrencyKey` column on `Jumoo_Pipelines`. An interactive pipeline left `Running` by a closed browser stops holding its key after `Jumoo:Processing:Pipelines:ConcurrencyKeyIdleTimeout` (default one hour). A background one stops holding its key once nothing will run it - no queue row left, or one out of attempts - and it has been quiet for a queue lease. The check and the save take the processing write lock, so two nodes can't both get the same key. - **"Already running" is a 409 everywhere.** `CreatePipeline`, `UpdatePipeline` and `ProcessPipeline` (resume) answer a held concurrency key with `409` and a `PipelineConflictProblemDetails` body - a `ProblemDetails` with the holder's `runningPipelineId` and the `concurrencyKey`, the same fields `StartPipeline`'s `409` carries. Every other failure is still a `400`. In the backoffice, `<jumoo-pipeline>` shows an inline "Already running" state (with the holder's status, when the user can see it) instead of an error toast over an empty modal, and fires `pipeline-conflict`. `getPipelineConflict(error)` reads the body off a failed request. - **Resume.** `IPipelineRunner.ResumeAsync(id, user, expectedAction)` moves a `Waiting` pipeline on, onto the processing queue, so the rest of the run needs no browser - for an action with `WaitOnAction` that waits on something outside the pipeline, such as an approval. Pass the action it should be waiting at, and a second resume is refused with the new `PipelineRunRejectedReason.NotWaiting`, so the run only moves on once. The status check, the concurrency key and the move to the queue are one write. A default interface member, so existing implementers still load. - **Pause, resume and finish notifications.** `PipelineWaitingNotification` when a top-level pipeline stops at an action that waits, `PipelineResumedNotification` (with who resumed it) from `ResumeAsync`, and `PipelineFinishedNotification` when one completes, fails or is cancelled. Each is raised once, by the processing that got the pipeline there. - **`ProcessingConstants` is public**, so packages can write `[ProcessingSwagger(ProcessingConstants.ApiName)]` rather than the literal `"processing"`. - **Run summaries.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetSummary(pipeline)` (default `null`) fills the status's `summary`. Register your own `IPipelineRunSummary` type with `AddPipelineRunSummaryType<T>()`.
### Changed
- **`@jumoo/processing` now publishes to npmjs.org**, not the Azure DevOps npm feed, which stops being anonymously readable in 2027. Pin the major you need (`^17`); nightlies are on the `next-17` dist-tag. Remove any `@jumoo:registry=` line from your `.npmrc`, then regenerate your lock file. - **Pipelines are private to the user who started them.** `PipelineProcessorBase.CanAccessPipeline` now allows the pipeline's creator or a member of the Umbraco admin group, rather than any backoffice user. Pipelines with no recorded owner stay open as before. Processors that override it and call `base` first inherit the change. - Options passed to `CreatePipeline` are applied before the pipeline is first saved, so the concurrency key is checked at create. - A step that posts to the background straight into an action with `WaitOnAction` now leaves the pipeline `Waiting`. It used to stay `Background` with nothing queued to run it. - A pipeline that stops at an action with `WaitOnAction` becomes a background request, wherever it was started: it is waiting on something outside it, not on the browser, so closing the `<jumoo-pipeline>` dialog no longer clears it. Actions with only an `Element` are unchanged.

item.title: uSync 18.1.5
item.description:
## Fixes
* Imported block values match what Umbraco publishes, so invariant block editors holding culture-variant elements no longer show pending changes after import (#1098) * Keep the published cache current after content type imports on Umbraco 18.0–18.1: refresh the types that use a changed composition, and treat variance-only changes as structural. No effect from Umbraco 18.2 on (#1102) * Export culture codes in standard casing (`da-DK`), so files no longer change when Umbraco is upgraded (#1101) * The uSync History client loads the uSync client by its package name, so it resolves on case-sensitive file systems (#1105)
## Build and CI
* Build the release, the nightly prerelease and the PR build once, in one job, on Linux (#1105) * Allow prerelease builds from any branch to publish to the nightly feed (#1099) * Stamp the nightly version as the informational version in prerelease builds (#1107) * Bump brace-expansion in usync-assets (#1100)
Forward merges from v17/main: #1103, #1104, #1106, #1108.
See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/blob/v18/main/CHANGELOG.md#1815---2026-09-30) for details.
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/compare/v18.1.4...v18.1.5

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 18.2.0
item.description:
## What's Changed * rc1 build (with improved Jumoo.Json core) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/1 * Document the move from Azure DevOps to GitHub by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/2 * CI safety net + repo hygiene (phases 1 and 2) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/3 * Versioning: make release/v* tags authoritative, migrate to GitVersion 6 by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/4 * Release from CI on a tag; retire the local packaging script by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/5 * Quality gates: coverage visibility, linting, C# formatting, npm audit by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/6 * Take the release version from the tag, so RCs work by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/7 * Treat an already-published npm version as success by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/8 * Publish NuGet packages to nuget.org via trusted publishing by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/9 * Update changelog for 18.1.0 by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/10 * Add cancellation token support and prune the pipeline cache table by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/16 * Merge v17/main into v18/main (2026-09-14) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/27 * Merge v17/main into v18/main (2026-09-24) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/30
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/compare/release/v17.4.2...release/v18.2.0
## What's Changed * rc1 build (with improved Jumoo.Json core) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/1 * Document the move from Azure DevOps to GitHub by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/2 * CI safety net + repo hygiene (phases 1 and 2) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/3 * Versioning: make release/v* tags authoritative, migrate to GitVersion 6 by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/4 * Release from CI on a tag; retire the local packaging script by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/5 * Quality gates: coverage visibility, linting, C# formatting, npm audit by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/6 * Take the release version from the tag, so RCs work by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/7 * Treat an already-published npm version as success by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/8 * Publish NuGet packages to nuget.org via trusted publishing by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/9 * Update changelog for 18.1.0 by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/10 * Add cancellation token support and prune the pipeline cache table by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/16 * Merge v17/main into v18/main (2026-09-14) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/27 * Merge v17/main into v18/main (2026-09-24) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/Jumoo/Jumoo.Processing/pull/30
